version.changelog:
video-generator-auto-post v1.0.0

- Initial release of the skill.
- Generate videos locally using ComfyUI with support for text-to-video, image-to-video, batch processing, and multiple video generation workflows.
- Automated posting to Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts.
- Includes scripts for single/batch generation, optimization, and social media auto-posting.
- Provides platform specifications, prompt guides, caption templates, and workflow examples.
- Offers troubleshooting tips and hardware/software requirements for smooth operation.

llm.summary: The skill's description (generate videos and auto-post) broadly matches the included instructions, but there are multiple inconsistencies and missing pieces (referenced scripts/assets not included, undeclared required credentials, and the posting code is unimplemented/TODO), so you should review and be cautious before using it or supplying credentials.

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose (local video generation + auto-posting) aligns with the SKILL.md instructions (install ComfyUI, models, generate videos, then post). However the skill references many scripts/assets (batch-generate.py, generate-video.py, caption-templates.md, assets/*.json) that are not present in the file manifest. That gap makes the package incomplete and reduces trust in what will actually run.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the user to edit ComfyUI's settings.json and to place API keys in a .env file and to pip-install social-media client libraries. Those actions are relevant to the declared purpose, but the included automation script (scripts/auto-post.py) only prints messages and contains TODO comments where network uploads should be implemented. The runtime instructions therefore promise automated posting but the shipped code does not implement it — an overpromise / incompleteness that could lead users to later add credentials or third‑party code without clear visibility.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only with a small script), so nothing is automatically downloaded or executed at install time. This is lower-risk from an installer perspective, but increases importance of reviewing and running the included scripts locally.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill metadata declares no required environment variables, yet the documentation and script comments instruct users to configure multiple social-platform API keys in a .env file (Twitter, TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube). Requesting those credentials would be proportionate to an auto-poster, but the manifest should declare them. Also the script reads environment via dotenv but currently does not actually use any credentials — the mismatch is confusing and could lead a user to supply sensitive tokens unnecessarily.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and does not modify other skills or system configurations beyond instructing the user to edit ComfyUI settings.json. It does not appear to attempt persistence or privilege escalation within the agent platform.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is incomplete and over-promises functionality: the README/skill doc references many scripts and assets that are not included, and the included auto-post script prints messages and has TODOs instead of actually uploading to social APIs. Before installing or putting any credentials into a .env file: (1) review the full code for any networking calls and ensure any upload implementation is trustworthy; (2) don't paste API keys/secrets until the code that uses them is present and reviewed; (3) be cautious editing ComfyUI settings.json — back up the file first; (4) if you need auto-posting, prefer a version that declares the required env vars and includes fully implemented, reviewed client code (or use official SDKs installed from trusted sources); (5) if the maintainer can provide the missing scripts/assets or a changelog explaining why those references are absent, that would reduce uncertainty and could change this assessment to benign.
